An attorney for CNN, MS Now and Politico told a federal judge today that the Trump administration
must be prevented from barring their reporters from the White House.
The news outlets argue that President Trump is punishing people for what they say and
violating the media outlets' First Amendment rights.
NPR's David Falkenflick has more.
You had Ted Butros, he's perhaps one of the most distinguished First Amendment litigators

the Smithsonian to preserve artifacts that he says reflect the corruption and authoritarianism
of the Trump presidencies.
And NPR's Frank Lenkfeit reports the bill's unlikely to pass and Trump would be all but
certain to veto it.
Representative Jamie Raskin, a Maryland Democrat, says objects would include the giant banner
of Trump hanging from the Department of Justice and be part of a future exhibit in the National
Museum of American History.
Raskin says it's important to document what he calls America's quote "descent into authoritarianism."
Trump has tried to recast the nation's capital in his own image.
He's also repeatedly denied being an authoritarian.
The president has also criticized how the Smithsonian depicts U.S. history.
The administration is preparing signs to warn visitors that the Smithsonian's leadership
is not telling the country's story accurately, but instead advancing what it calls "personal
radical ideologies."
Frank Lenkfeit, NPR News, Washington.
France's education minister today proposed solutions to the school crisis that has rocked
the country.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports his proposals came as high school students gathered in cities
across the country for a second big day of rallies in what is now their weeks-long push
for better conditions in schools.
Some 25,000 high schoolers rallied in Paris' Place de la Bastille.
They were joined by college students and some parents, teachers and union members.
The rallies were smaller than Mondays, and more violent.
Police charged to clear the plaza.
There was tear gas, and some 500 people were arrested.
Hours later, French education minister Edouard Gefre spoke on television.
He says there will be immediate help for 500 schools in real difficulty.
In the next hours, we will send 3,000 replacement teachers to these schools, he said, calling
it the first part of a bigger plan.
But the plan has not stopped the students from calling for another day of nationwide
protests next Tuesday.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
The U.S. stock market closed mixed today, the NASDAQ fell one and a quarter percent.
This is NPR News.
Ukrainian military commanders say a shortage of combat-ready troops is increasingly acute
as Russia's war drags into a fifth year.
Some units are at only half strength, and there aren't enough forces to fully exploit
advantages brought by Ukraine's recent drone innovations.
Military experts say draft dodging and desertion remain major challenges.
OpenAI has banned Russian and Iranian accounts that, among other things, used chat GPT to

Those events angered a Polish member of the European Parliament.
The whole thing stoked tensions between Poland and Ukraine, which aligns with Kremlin schools.
In a different case, operatives from Iran made up fake authors to pitch articles to
small media outlets around the world, and published almost a hundred articles in this
way.
OpenAI says these internal reports show that for influence campaigns, tricking established
outlets into spreading the message can be far more effective than simply creating fake
accounts on social media.
Hua Jignan, NPR News.
